questions.q:
Given below are two statements
Statement I : A catalyst cannot alter the equilibrium constant \left(\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}\right)$ of the reaction, temperature remaining constant
Statement II : A homogenous catalyst can change the equilibrium composition of a system temperature remaining constant
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below$
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II is false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Statement I is true because a catalyst increases the rate of both the forward and backward reactions to the same extent. Therefore, it does not affect the equilibrium constant ($K_c$) of the reaction. The equilibrium constant depends only on temperature.

Statement II is false because a catalyst, whether homogeneous or heterogeneous, does not alter the equilibrium composition of a reaction mixture. It only reduces the time required for the system to attain equilibrium.

Therefore, Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

Answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.q:
For the given reaction, choose the correct expression of ${K}_{C}$ from the following:

${Fe}^{3 +} \left($aq\right) + {SCN}^{-} \left($aq\right) ⇌ ( FeSCN{)}^{2 +}$\left($aq\right)$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The equilibrium constant of a chemical reaction (usually denoted by the symbol K) provides insight into the relationship between the products and reactants when a chemical reaction reaches equilibrium. For example, the equilibrium constant of concentration (denoted by Kc) of a chemical reaction at equilibrium can be defined as the ratio of the concentration of products to the concentration of the reactants, each raised to their respective stoichiometric coefficients. It is important to note that there are different types of equilibrium constants that provide relationships between the products and the reactants of equilibrium reactions in terms of different units.

Equilibrium Constant Formula

${K}_{eqb} = \dfrac{Kf}{Kb} = \dfrac{\left[C\right]c\left[D\right]d}{\left[A\right]a\left[B\right]b} = {K}_{c}$

Where ${K}_{c}$ indicates the equilibrium constant measured in moles per litre.

${K}_{C} = \dfrac{ \left[\text{ Products }\right]}${ \left[Reactants\right]}$

${K}_{C} = \left[{FeSCN}^{2 +}\right] \left[{Fe}^{3 +}\right] \left[{SCN}^{-}\right]$

Hence, the answer is option A.

$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given that concentration of& ${A}_{2}{B}_{3}$~is~$C$~and degree of dissociation is~$\alpha$

The equilibrium reaction of weak electrolyte~${A}_{2}{B}_{3}$~is

$\begin{cases}{A}_{2}{B}_{3} & ⇌ 2A^{3 +} & + 3B^{2 -} \\ C & - & - \\ ↓ & ↓ & ↓ \\ C ( 1 - \alpha ) & 2C\alpha & 3C\alpha\end{cases}$

Now,~The equilibrium constant is the ratio of the concentrations of reactants and products raised to the stoichiometric coefficients.

${K}_{eq} = \dfrac{( 2C \alpha{)}^{2} ( 3C \alpha{)}^{3}}{C ( 1 - \alpha )} = 108C^{4}{α}^{5}$

$\dfrac{Keq}{108C^{4}} = {α}^{5} ⇒ \alpha = \left(\dfrac{Keq}{108C^{4}}\right)\dfrac{1}{5}$

questions.q: In the following system, $\mathrm{PCl}_5(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_3(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{~g})$ at equilibrium, upon addition of xenon gas at constant $\mathrm{T} \ \text{ and } \mathrm{p}$, the concentration of
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $PCl_5(g) \rightleftharpoons PCl_3(g) + Cl_2(g)$.

When an inert gas like xenon is added at constant temperature and pressure, the total volume of the system must increase to maintain constant pressure.

According to Le Chatelier's principle, an increase in volume causes the equilibrium to shift in the direction that produces a greater number of gaseous moles. Since $\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = 1$, the equilibrium shifts in the forward direction, increasing the number of moles of $PCl_3$ and $Cl_2$ and decreasing the number of moles of $PCl_5$.

However, the concentration is defined as the number of moles divided by the total volume ($C = \dfrac{n}{V}$).

The equilibrium constant is $K_c = \dfrac{[PCl_3][Cl_2]}{[PCl_5]}$.

Because the moles of $PCl_5$ decrease and the volume increases, the concentration of $PCl_5$ definitively decreases.

For $K_c$ to remain constant at a given temperature, the product of the concentrations of the products, $[PCl_3][Cl_2]$, must also decrease. This implies that the effect of the volume expansion outweighs the increase in the number of moles for the products.

Therefore, the overall concentrations of all species, including $PCl_3$ and $Cl_2$, will decrease.

This corresponds to option (2). ;

questions.q:
The number of correct statement/s involving equilibria in physical processes from the following is ________

(A) Equilibrium is possible only in a closed system at a given temperature.

(B) Both the opposing processes occur at the same rate.

(C) When equilibrium is attained at a given temperature, the value of all its parameters became equal

(D) For dissolution of solids in liquids, the solubility is constant at a given temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The equilibrium is possible when there is no exchange of matter between system and surroundings.

At equilibrium state the forward and backward processes occur with same rate (speed)

When a system reaches equilibrium at a given temperature, the forward and reverse reactions are occurring at the same rate, and the concentrations (or partial pressures) of the reactants and products no longer change with time. At this point, the system has achieved a steady state, where the rate of the forward reaction is equal to the rate of the reverse reaction. So when equilibrium is attained, the value of all its parameters became constant.

The solubility is function of solubility product, the value of which is constant at a given temperature.
